gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-beng: Noto Sans Bengali keeps its capitals barely above the lowercase and leaves every letter mouth wide open. Noto Sans Bengali would carry a long passage easily, while Blockletter's bent-copper-pipe strokes stay up in the heading.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-bhai: Smooth, pencil-drawn tallness up top, with no pinched joints or flared ends. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki follows with tightly coiled, rope-like lowercase and open apertures, so a long passage keeps moving without a snag.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-brah: Outlined letters, one steady line, a squat belly. Noto Sans Brahmi sets its mean line high and leaves every curve open-ended, which gives Blockletter a lighter, more modern sans-serif partner to lean against.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-bugi:
Blockletter draws every letter with one stroke width.
Noto Sans Buginese keeps its ascenders short and its letter mouths open like unjoined chalk arcs, so a longer stretch of text reads easily and without fuss.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-buhi: Glass tubing bent into letters, with a tall, squat-bellied build. Noto Sans Buhid sits beneath it, and its high x-height and generous gaps between curve ends and stems keep the sans quiet next to that heading.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-cari: Noto Sans Carian keeps its terminals apart like open scissor blades, with only tiny gaps under the ascender tops. Blockletter's constant stroke weight, free of any sparkle, is what makes the pair distinct.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-chak:
Blockletter traces its letters like a single thick thread.
Noto Sans Chakma does the opposite job, packing lowercase up toward the caps and keeping its s and c mouths uncrowded, where the heading is built to be looked at.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-cham: Laser-etched, constant-width lines with a tall, brush-pen belly. Blockletter is best at being a striking heading, while Noto Sans Cham's tall rounded lowercase and roomy open c shapes make it the one to read.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-cher: Noto Sans Cherokee gives a tall band of letters with short stalks above and a wide gap at the e. And Blockletter, with stroke ends that look cut from one ribbon, leaves a longer passage feeling approachable underneath it.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-chor: A neon-tube track, one width, drawn with pencil-like restraint. Blockletter is best at that precise, striking heading, while Noto Sans Chorasmian does its best work with a large x-height, short ascenders and curves that stop short.
